A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same SPIA research work. Their complete 36-page contents, including figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–G, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original anonymization experiments on TAB and PANORAMA in Table 4, eleven-model inference validation in Table 9, and supplementary empirical analyses in Appendix E.

after.justification: v2 retains these original anonymization experiments, inference-validation results, and supplementary analyses. Retained results qualify as original empirical evidence.

M1.justification: SPIA's subject identification, subject-wise PII inference, matching, and scoring procedures remain unchanged. The new Figure 12 illustrates the pipeline already documented in Section 4.2 and Appendix C.3.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same English legal documents from TAB and online texts from PANORAMA, covering the same 15 PII categories and subject-level privacy tasks. No dataset, domain, or test scenario is added.

E2.justification: The evaluated methods remain TAB Longformer, DeID-GPT, DP-Prompt, and Adversarial Anonymization, with the same six backbones for generative methods. The inference-validation and multi-adversary comparisons also retain their comparator sets.

E3.justification: The TAB/PANORAMA test sets remain 144/151 documents. Certainty filtering, top-1 inference, evaluator models, matching rules, scoring thresholds, anonymization settings, and privacy/utility metrics are unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix E retains the same adversary-robustness, PII-type, hardness, privacy–utility, and backbone-behavior analyses. Figure 12 supplies illustrative protocol examples without adding empirical analysis.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is unchanged, including Table 11's rank correlations, n=38, and p<10^-26 reporting. Neither version adds or revises repeated-run, seed, confidence-interval, or uncertainty-estimation information relative to the other.

E6.justification: Reported results match throughout the tables and retained plots. For example, Table 4 retains CPR 0.330 for Longformer on TAB and 0.870 for Adversarial Anonymization with GPT-4.1 on PANORAMA.

T1.justification: The CPR/IPR definitions in Equations 1–2 and the worked calculation in Appendix C.3.3 are unchanged. Figure 12 repeats the existing CPR formula and scoring scheme without introducing mathematical reasoning or definitions.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same benchmark contributions and claims about masking overestimating protection, non-target subjects' exposure, and domain-dependent anonymization effectiveness.

C2.justification: The domain and backbone explanations, privacy–utility interpretations, and limitations concerning collective references, equal PII weighting, subject attribution, language, and dataset scope are retained unchanged.

D1.justification: Implementation settings, model versions, hardware, annotation instructions, prompt templates, and code/data access statements remain unchanged. The added diagram restates documented evaluation steps.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, bibliography, benchmark positioning, and novelty claims are unchanged. Figure 12 repeats the existing attribution of the scoring scheme to Staab et al. (2024).

P1.justification: Appendix C.3 adds a short passage introducing the protocol overview. Figure references and the arXiv version/date stamp are updated; the section organization and remaining prose are preserved.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figure 12 on page 20, illustrating subject matching, PII scoring, and CPR calculation. Existing Figures 12–29 become Figures 13–30, with appendix page reflow. Existing tables and result graphics are retained.

improvement.justification: The added Figure 12 brings the previously documented evaluation steps into one visual explanation, showing matched and unmatched subjects, scoring examples, and CPR aggregation. This modestly improves clarity of the central evaluation framework while preserving the scientific content and evidence.
